quarterly_data.signal: Quantinuum prospectus, ownership and research: as of March 31, 2026 Honeywell was the controlling majority owner with an overall 55% ownership in the business, pre-existing Cambridge Quantum shareholders 34% and several minority investors 11%; upon completion of the offering the Honeywell Entities hold approximately 47.8% of the combined voting power of Class A and Class B common stock. Quantinuum, through subsidiaries, collaborates with NTESS (National Technology and Engineering Solutions of Sandia, the Honeywell subsidiary that manages and operates Sandia National Laboratories) under three statements of work in integrated photonics, quantum performance benchmarking and validation, and quantum error correction, providing cost-reimbursable funding.

connects_to.relationship: fabrication of ion traps for Quantinuum quantum computers (2026 SSSA, ten-year term)

contracts.signal: Quantinuum prospectus: under the 2026 SSSA, AERO may not sell or supply ion traps to any party other than Quantinuum for use within the field of quantum computing for six years from the agreement's effective date, while Quantinuum may buy ion traps from other suppliers without restriction; AERO is reimbursed at its government bid rate plus a 15% mark-up, owns unit-process and manufacturing-control intellectual property (licensed royalty-free to Quantinuum within quantum computing) and Quantinuum owns process-flow, product-design and device-control IP; either party may terminate on 24 months' notice before a term expires. Under the prior 2021 SSSA with Honeywell, Quantinuum paid $3.2 million in each of 2025 and 2024 and $3.6 million in 2023.
contracts.units: six-year exclusivity for ion traps in quantum computing
